seo.description: Visit Safi’s National Ceramics Museum: collections, hours mindset and how it complements the potters’ quarter.
seo.og_description: See the best of Safi and Moroccan ceramics in one museum stop.

name: National Ceramics Museum
hero_subtitle: The national collection that explains Safi’s craft reputation.

overview.title: Context for the craft
overview.p1: The National Ceramics Museum in Safi gathers historical and regional pieces that explain why the city became Morocco’s pottery capital.
overview.p2: Displays cover techniques, styles and the link between local clay and the famous blue and polychrome ware.
overview.p3: Visit after or before the potters’ quarter: the museum gives context; the hill shows living practice.

q1.question: Is there an entry fee?
q1.answer: Yes — it is a ticketed museum. Keep small change or a card.

q2.question: How long should I stay?
q2.answer: 45 to 90 minutes covers the main rooms without rushing.

q3.question: Is it suitable for children?
q3.answer: Yes for a short visit; the potters’ quarter is often more interactive for kids.

q4.question: Can I take photos?
q4.answer: Follow on-site rules; flash is often restricted.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Optional. Labels and the collection are clear enough for a self-guided visit.
